entries.reason: task-139 post-merge gms_v92 correlate of the cash-item-use-pet-skill coverage sweep (IDA session acdfccff, GMS_v92_1_DEVM.exe.i64). The original sweep covered the eight GMS versions in scope at the time (v48/v61/v72/v79/v83/v84/v87/v95); gms_v92 was excluded on the then-true premise that its template routed no pet handlers, which merging main invalidated. This entry closes that gap. CWvsContext::SendConsumeCashItemUseRequest @0x9bfe10 (size 0x501a) builds the common header BEFORE the switch: COutPacket(0x56=86, matching this version's registry opcode 86) @0x9bfed5, Encode4(time)@0x9bfef2, Encode2(nPOS)@0x9bff03, Encode4(nItemID)@0x9bff14. It then switches on get_consume_cash_item_type(itemId) (sub_498640) with base 12 ('add eax, 0FFFFFFF4h' @0x9bff23, 'switch 62 cases'), range check 'cmp eax, 3Dh' / 'ja def_9BFF39' @0x9bff2c, byte index table byte_9C4ECC @0x9c4ecc, jump table jpt_9BFF39 @0x9c4e2c. Type 28 IS uniquely dispatched — 28 does NOT appear in the compiler's default-case list (cases 35,36,38,39,41,43,45,54-59,62,67-69), and resolving it through both tables gives index 28-12=16 -> byte_9C4ECC[16]=0x0e -> jpt_9BFF39[14]=0x9c4dfe (label loc_9C4DFE). Control for the table arithmetic: jpt_9BFF39[0x27]=0x9c00b5, which is exactly the def_9BFF39 label the disassembly names, so the index math is confirmed rather than assumed. The FULL body of the case-28 arm is seven instructions: lea ecx,[esp+234h+var_200] @0x9c4dfe (var_200 at this esp base is the SAME address as the ctor's [esp+238h+var_204], i.e. the COutPacket itself); mov byte ptr [esp+234h+var_4], bl @0x9c4e02; call sub_42B500 @0x9c4e09 (0x1f bytes — the COutPacket destructor, not a sender); lea ecx,[esp+234h+arg_C] @0x9c4e0e; mov [esp+234h+var_4], 0FFFFFFFFh @0x9c4e15; call sub_403900 @0x9c4e20 (0x11 bytes — ZXString destructor); jmp loc_9C00E7 @0x9c4e25. loc_9C00E7 @0x9c00e7 is the function's OWN EPILOGUE (mov large fs:0, ecx; pop ecx/edi/esi/ebp/ebx; add esp, 220h; retn 10h). There is no Encode1/2/4/8, EncodeBuffer or EncodeStr call anywhere in the arm, and neither SendPacket (@0x42a7a0) nor CClientSocket::SendPacket (@0x4ac120) is reachable from it. The arm is a behavioural clone of the default case at def_9BFF39 @0x9c00b5, which likewise runs the COutPacket destructor into the same epilogue. Net effect: selecting a type-28 cash item on gms_v92 sends NOTHING on the wire — not even the common header. Sibling cross-check (VERIFYING_A_PACKET 'Is this cell n-a?' step 3): the separate cash-SLOT dispatcher CWvsContext::SendCashSlotItemUseRequest @0x9d1010 — the structural analog for locker-SN items — dispatches only types 8 (SendActivatePetRequest), 9 (SendActiveEffectItemChange), 11 (SendEntrustedShopCheckRequest) and 38 (SendRemoteShopOpenRequest); it has no pet-skill-teach arm. Receive-side note: GW_ItemSlotPet::RawDecode @0x4f0820 DOES read usPetSkill into the secured pair +81/+85 on v92, but that is the shared pet-item serialization present on every GMS version including the seven already recorded n-a here, and per design 1.1 GMS clients consume usPetSkill only via the auto-speaking path, never to teach a pouch skill — so its presence is not evidence of a send arm. Structural note, answering the open question left in docs/tasks/task-139-pet-auto-pot-validation/cash-item-use-pet-skill-coverage.md ('a structural signal worth remembering if a v92 correlate is ever checked'): v92 resembles v95 in that a case value IS allocated for type 28 via a real uniquely-targeted label rather than folded into default (unlike v72/v79/v83/v84/v87), but it is behaviourally identical to every other GMS version — nothing is sent. Recorded n-a rather than left incomplete because there is no payload a future verify pass could ever fixture from this arm.
